item.title: Revisiting theoretical pillars of HRM in the age of uncertainty: Contributions for performance
item.content:encoded:
Organizations face unprecedented challenges from uncertainty, technological change, and shifting work arrangements. This special issue calls for researchers to revisit fundamental HRM theories and examine whether established assumptions adequately explain the relationship between people, organizations, and performance in today's turbulent context. The issue seeks to move beyond incremental complexity by returning to core concepts and critically assessing whether traditional perspectives on HRM-strategy alignment, employee development, and performance outcomes remain sufficient.

The special issue welcomes theoretically grounded and methodologically rigorous contributions that challenge conventional HRM wisdom and propose new understandings relevant to uncertain environments. Research may address tensions and unintended consequences of HRM practices, sustainability concerns, digitalization, employee well-being, and emerging employment models. Empirical studies, conceptual papers, and literature reviews are all welcome, provided they offer clear advances to HRM theory and research.

Appel publié par Journal of Organizational Effectiveness People and Performance. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.

  • Sustainable HRM, green HRM, and long-term organizational performance

item.title: Unpacking Digitalization: Antecedents, Strategies, and Performance Implications
item.content:encoded:
Jasmina Berbegal-Mirabent, Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya

Angelo Cavallo, Politecnico di Milano

Antje Fiedler, University of Auckland

Esteban Lafuente, Instituto Tecnológico de Costa Rica

Digital transformation has become essential for both private and public organizations seeking innovation and competitive advantage. However, the literature lacks coherent understanding of how digitalization is implemented across different contexts. While large organizations traditionally led these efforts, SMEs and public institutions increasingly must engage in digital transformation despite significant resource constraints.

The relationship between digitalization and performance is complex and context-dependent. Digital technologies offer opportunities for innovation and efficiency but also carry risks of misalignment with strategy and organizational disruption. Success requires aligning digital initiatives with organizational capabilities, workforce skills, and strategic planning rather than technology adoption alone.

This special issue seeks contributions examining how organizations manage digitalization efforts across private firms and public institutions, addressing the drivers of digital transformation, mechanisms through which digitalization influences performance outcomes, and how digital transformation reshapes competitive dynamics in different economic contexts.

Appel publié par Review of Managerial Science. Voir l'appel sur le site de l'éditeur. Fiche de l'appel sur kerostig.
